newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate lower, baht rises late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate lower, baht rises late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 9.25-9.50 percent in late trade on Thursday from 9.50 percent early on steadily rising liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said the money supply continued to rise following heavy selling of the dollar in foreign exchange markets over the past few days.
"The interbank rate is quite stable today. The central bank appeared to stabilise the rate through its bond repurchase operation," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
An announcement by the central bank that it would increase the amount of its 28-day bond to be auctioned on Friday by 1.5 billion baht had little impact on the market, dealers said.
The baht was stronger at 25.658-25.663 to the dollar late from 25.665-25.670 in the morning on dollar selling, dealers said.
"Some players continued to sell the dollar today. The U.S unit's narrow movement abroad prompted some profit taking on its recent rise," said another dealer.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted unchanged at 8.50/9.00 satang in late trade.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.67 against a 56-month low of 25.69 on Wednesday .
